units.api: ShellOutput accessors on a resolved result: (await $`echo hi`).text() === "hi\n"; (await $`echo '{"hello": 123}'`).json() deep-equals {hello: 123}; (await $`echo hello`).blob() equals new Blob([new TextEncoder().encode("hello")]) (bun:test Blob equality; the actual blob holds "hello\n").

With $.throws(true), the rejected ShellError exposes the same output accessors as ShellOutput: for $`echo hi; ls oogabooga` err.stderr.toString() === "ls: oogabooga: No such file or directory\n" and err.text() === "hi\n"; for $`echo '{"hello": 123}'; ls oogabooga` err.json() deep-equals {hello: 123}; for $`echo hello; ls oogabooga` err.blob() equals new Blob([new TextEncoder().encode("hello")]). The error must be defined (the promise rejects).

units.upstream: a capture of 2^32 + 1 bytes rejects with the RangeError that new ArrayBuffer(2 ** 32 + 1) throws
units.api: Only when posix and total memory >= 16 GiB (upstream describe.skipIf): in a child process, `await Bun.$`head -c ${String(2 ** 32 + 1)} /dev/zero`.quiet()` must REJECT (not crash/abort) with an error that is `instanceof RangeError` and has message "Out of memory"; the child prints that and exits 0 with empty stderr and no signal. Captured stdout larger than the max Buffer length (2^32 bytes) cannot be handed to JS.
units.note: crash regression at the JS Buffer length limit; needs 4-8 GiB RAM and a 2 min timeout, so not turned into a corpus case
